# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 15 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 15 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_015_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 7

**1** "Why was she shown to me as an aged woman in the former vision and now as a young woman?" **2** She replied: "Listen. The reason she was shown as an aged woman in the first two visions is that your spirit was old and already withering away, and it had no power on account of your infirmities and doubts. **3** For just as an aged person — one who has no more hope of growing young again — expects nothing but to pass away, so also you who were weakened by the cares of this life had given up on yourselves and were not being refreshed by the Lord. But after he had spoken to you through me, and you had turned your hearts toward him, you were refreshed and laid aside your infirmity, and so strength came to you and you grew young again. **4** And when you see the tower made into one solid stone, this also shall come to pass: those who have believed sincerely will all be made one — one body, one mind, one spirit, one faith, one love. And then the tower will be built, and all will rejoice together." **5** "I would also like to know," I said, "why the stones that were dragged from the deep sea and placed in the building are in accord with the ones that came from dry land." **6** "Because they heard and believed," she said. "Those who were dragged from the sea were tested by fire, while those from dry land did not need such testing."

---

*EMET note: The Church's age-to-youth transformation is explained: it mirrors the community's spiritual condition. As the people repent, the Church grows younger. The tower-as-one-stone eschatology echoes Eph 4:4-6.*
